gen-gf-turret-road-gf-telex: Telex has curvy, loosened letters that feel like they've slipped out of a clamp. Telex over a long page stays easygoing, a plain sans that never fusses while Turret Road's stencil-cut strokes handle the shouting.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-tenor-sans: Tenor Sans reads contemporary and quiet, its faint stroke variation and well-spaced c tips giving each line a soft, restrained texture. Over a long passage it stays gentle, while Turret Road's wirelike strokes stand firmly apart.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-tirra: Round and bold, Turret Road curves like open parentheses, drawn in a tube-like line that never changes width. And Tirra repeats those parenthesis curves in a modern sans-serif, so heading and text feel like relatives.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-titillium-web: Titillium Web keeps its stroke ends set far apart, which gives text a contemporary, approachable looseness. Titillium Web over a long passage feels friendly and unhurried, a plain sans next to Turret Road's skimming, constant-weight heading.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-tomorrow: Neon-tube lettering, round and commanding. Turret Road is best at making a loud first impression, while Tomorrow, a neutral sans-serif with bowls like cupped clay, is best at quietly carrying everything after it.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-trispace: Turret Road lays its letters out like spaghetti, round and bold, with a pen-like line that never thins. Make that heading small or Trispace large and the loose, outward-curving text starts competing with it.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-tsukimi-rounded: Tsukimi Rounded reads clean and softly rounded, with parallel stroke edges. Over a long passage it feels steady and smooth, a sans-serif that lets Turret Road's parenthesis-round heading stay the bold one.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-tuffy: Bold, round, and unmistakably Turret Road, drawn with a pen that never changes pressure. But Tuffy has the quieter job, a professional sans sketched in pencil, with a widely parted s that keeps text easy going.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-urbanist: Turret Road's constant pen-like line makes round forms that read like open parentheses. Urbanist, a plain sans with a broad-nibbed stroke that never curls shut, is built to carry the reading while the heading commands attention.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-varela: Round forms like open parentheses give Turret Road its bold, commanding stamp, all in one pen-like weight. Varela does the follow-through, a modern sans-serif whose wide-mouthed c shapes and one-width t keep the text approachable.
